title: World Capitals, Megacities & Urban Geography
description: Comprehensive 60-question urban expedition exploring planned capitals, high-altitude metropolises, historic citadels, sprawling megacities, and demographic records.

questions.question: Which planned capital city was designed in the shape of a massive airplane by urban planner Lúcio Costa and inaugurated in 1960?
questions.explanation: Brasília was constructed in the interior Brazilian highlands with landmark modernist administrative buildings designed by Oscar Niemeyer.

questions.question: In 2005, which Southeast Asian nation officially transferred its administrative capital from Yangon to the purpose-built city of Naypyidaw?
questions.explanation: Naypyidaw was developed inland as a sprawling, planned administrative center with twenty-lane boulevards and expansive ministry zones.

questions.question: Which national capital was planned by American architect Walter Burley Griffin as a compromise between two rival cities?
questions.explanation: Canberra was chosen and designed as the federal capital of Australia situated in a purpose-built territory between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Which West African nation moved its official federal capital from coastal Lagos to the centrally located planned city of Abuja in 1991?
questions.explanation: Abuja was selected for its geographic centrality and neutral ethnic positioning, dominated by the colossal monolith Zuma Rock.

questions.question: Which planned capital city replaced Karachi as the permanent seat of government in Pakistan during the 1960s?
questions.explanation: Islamabad was designed by Greek urban planner Constantinos Doxiadis in a grid-like sector layout near the Margalla Hills.

questions.question: In what year was Brasília officially inaugurated as the new federal capital of Brazil?
questions.explanation: President Juscelino Kubitschek officially inaugurated Brasília on April 21, 1960, replacing Rio de Janeiro as the national seat of power.

questions.question: Which city is the highest administrative national capital in the world, sitting over 3,600 meters above sea level in an Andean canyon?
questions.explanation: La Paz serves as the seat of Bolivia executive and legislative branches, nestled within a dramatic canyon beneath Mount Illimani.

questions.question: Which South American capital city is situated just twenty-five kilometers south of the Equator on the slopes of the active Pichincha volcano?
questions.explanation: Quito is the capital of Ecuador and one of the highest national capitals on Earth at roughly 2,850 meters elevation.

questions.question: Which national capital is recognized as the coldest capital city on Earth by annual mean temperature?
questions.explanation: Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia experiences extreme subarctic continental winters, with average January temperatures plunging below minus twenty degrees Celsius.

questions.question: What is the northernmost capital city of an independent sovereign nation on Earth?
questions.explanation: Reykjavik in Iceland sits at approximately 64 degrees 08 minutes North latitude, making it the most northerly sovereign capital.

questions.question: Which city holds the distinction of being the southernmost national capital in the world?
questions.explanation: Wellington at the southern tip of New Zealand North Island sits at approximately 41 degrees 17 minutes South latitude.

questions.question: What is the approximate elevation in meters above sea level of La Paz, the world highest administrative capital?
questions.explanation: La Paz sits at an average altitude of approximately 3,640 meters, while its adjoining sister city El Alto exceeds 4,000 meters.

questions.question: Which country has three official capital cities dividing administrative, legislative, and judicial powers across Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein?
questions.explanation: South Africa distributes national power among Pretoria as executive, Cape Town as legislative, and Bloemfontein as judicial capitals.

questions.question: What historic city is recognized in the national constitution as the historic constitutional capital of Bolivia, where the supreme court sits?
questions.explanation: Sucre is the constitutional and judicial capital of Bolivia, while La Paz houses the national congress and presidential palace.

questions.question: Although Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands, in which city do the parliament and royal court reside?
questions.explanation: The Hague has served as the actual seat of Dutch government, parliament, supreme court, and diplomatic embassies since the late sixteenth century.

questions.question: Which sovereign microstate capital is perched dramatically on the three peaks of Mount Titano in the Apennine Mountains?
questions.explanation: The City of San Marino crowns Mount Titano with its three iconic medieval fortress towers Guaita, Cesta, and Montale.

questions.question: Which sovereign city-state is completely enclosed within the municipal boundaries of Rome?
questions.explanation: Vatican City was established as an independent sovereign enclave inside Rome via the 1929 Lateran Treaty with Italy.

questions.question: How many official capital cities does the Republic of South Africa maintain to balance power across its provinces?
questions.explanation: South Africa designates Pretoria for the executive branch, Cape Town for the parliament, and Bloemfontein for the judicial supreme court.

questions.question: Which metropolitan area is the most populous continuous urban agglomeration in the world with over 37 million residents?
questions.explanation: The Greater Tokyo metropolitan region in the Kanto Plain encompasses Tokyo, Yokohama, Kawasaki, and Chiba with over 37 million people.

questions.question: Due to land subsidence and severe flooding, which Southeast Asian nation is constructing a replacement capital named Nusantara in East Kalimantan?
questions.explanation: Jakarta on Java is sinking rapidly due to groundwater extraction, prompting Indonesia to build the smart forest city Nusantara on Borneo.

questions.question: Which Indian megacity, formerly known as Bombay, is the commercial capital of India built across seven interconnected islands?
questions.explanation: Mumbai was formed by joining seven historic islands via extensive colonial land reclamation schemes throughout the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

questions.question: What sovereign island city-state is connected to the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula by the Johor-Singapore Causeway?
questions.explanation: Singapore transformed from a British colonial trading post into one of the world wealthiest global financial hubs and maritime ports.

questions.question: Which Asian megacity region forms the world largest continuous manufacturing and urban megaregion around the mouth of the Pearl River?
questions.explanation: The Pearl River Delta combines Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Dongguan, Foshan, Hong Kong, and Macao into a powerhouse urban zone.

questions.question: Approximately how many million people reside within the Greater Tokyo Area, making it the most populous urban region on Earth?
questions.explanation: Demographic surveys estimate the Greater Tokyo metropolitan population at approximately 37.4 million residents.

questions.question: Which historic city served as the imperial capital and residence of the Emperor of Japan for over a thousand years before Tokyo?
questions.explanation: Kyoto, originally named Heian-kyo, served as the formal seat of the imperial court from 794 until the Meiji Restoration in 1868.

questions.question: Which city on the Rhine River served as the federal capital of West Germany from 1949 until German reunification?
questions.explanation: Bonn was selected by Chancellor Konrad Adenauer as the provisional federal capital of the Federal Republic of Germany.

questions.question: Which major southeastern city served as the national capital of Brazil for nearly two centuries prior to the founding of Brasília?
questions.explanation: Rio de Janeiro was the capital of Portuguese America and Brazil from 1763 until the federal administration relocated inland in 1960.

questions.question: What city was the capital of Kazakhstan from its independence in 1991 until the government relocated north to Astana in 1997?
questions.explanation: Almaty remains Kazakhstan largest metropolis and cultural hub despite the administrative move to Astana.

questions.question: Which ancient metropolis on the Bosporus served as the capital of the Ottoman Empire for nearly five centuries before Ankara was chosen in 1923?
questions.explanation: Following the Turkish War of Independence, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk declared Ankara the national capital of the new Turkish Republic.

questions.question: In what year did Kazakhstan officially transfer its national capital from Almaty to the northern city of Astana?
questions.explanation: President Nursultan Nazarbayev officially proclaimed Akmola, soon renamed Astana, as the national capital on December 10, 1997.

questions.question: Which Canadian city on the border of Ontario and Quebec was chosen by Queen Victoria in 1857 as the national capital?
questions.explanation: Ottawa was selected as a defensible inland compromise situated between English-speaking Upper Canada and French-speaking Lower Canada.

questions.question: What Argentine capital city is located along the southwestern shore of the vast Río de la Plata estuary?
questions.explanation: Buenos Aires is the political and cultural capital of Argentina, famous for its historic Plaza de Mayo and colorful La Boca district.

questions.question: Which South American capital city is situated in a central valley encircled by the towering peaks of the Andes and the Chilean Coastal Range?
questions.explanation: Santiago was founded in 1541 by Pedro de Valdivia alongside the Mapocho River in the central Chilean valley.

questions.question: Which high-altitude Andean capital city sits on the Sabana de Bogotá plateau at roughly 2,640 meters above sea level?
questions.explanation: Bogotá is the sprawling capital of Colombia, featuring the historic colonial center La Candelaria beneath Monserrate mountain.

questions.question: What Caribbean capital city was founded by Spanish colonists in 1521, featuring massive coastal fortifications named El Morro and San Cristóbal?
questions.explanation: San Juan in Puerto Rico is the oldest European-founded city under United States jurisdiction with grand colonial walls.

questions.question: What is the average elevation in meters above sea level of Bogotá, the capital of Colombia?
questions.explanation: Bogotá sits on a high Andean plateau at roughly 2,640 meters altitude, making it the third-highest national capital in South America.

questions.question: Which iconic river divides the Hungarian capital into the hilly, historic Buda district on the west bank and the flat Pest district on the east?
questions.explanation: Buda, Pest, and Óbuda were unified in 1873 to form modern Budapest, connected by landmark spans such as the Széchenyi Chain Bridge.

questions.question: Which Central European capital city on the Vltava River is celebrated worldwide as the City of a Hundred Spires?
questions.explanation: Prague in the Czech Republic features the ancient Charles Bridge, the historic Astronomical Clock, and the expansive Prague Castle complex.

questions.question: Which Nordic capital city is constructed across an archipelago of fourteen islands where Lake Mälaren flows into the Baltic Sea?
questions.explanation: Stockholm in Sweden is often called the Venice of the North, linked by over fifty bridges across scenic waterways.

questions.question: Which European capital is located at the mouth of the Tagus River, featuring the historic Belem Tower and the steep Alfama quarter?
questions.explanation: Lisbon is the westernmost capital city in mainland Europe, built across seven steep hills overlooking the Tagus estuary.

questions.question: Which inland capital city is situated on the Manzanares River at the exact geographic center of the Iberian Peninsula?
questions.explanation: King Philip II relocated the Spanish royal court to Madrid in 1561, establishing it as the permanent political heart of Spain.

questions.question: Across how many primary islands is the Swedish capital city of Stockholm built?
questions.explanation: Stockholm spans 14 main islands connected by over 50 bridges where Lake Mälaren empties into the Baltic archipelago.

questions.question: What megacity along the Nile River is the largest metropolitan area in Egypt and the wider Arab world?
questions.explanation: Cairo was founded in 969 CE by the Fatimid dynasty and sits immediately adjacent to the ancient Giza Necropolis.

questions.question: Which sprawling Nigerian megacity situated on coastal lagoons is the largest urban center and financial engine in Sub-Saharan Africa?
questions.explanation: Lagos expanded rapidly across Lagos Island, Victoria Island, and the mainland to house over twenty million residents.

questions.question: Which East African capital city, known as the Green City in the Sun, is famous for hosting a wild game national park right against its city skyline?
questions.explanation: Nairobi National Park borders the city limits of the Kenyan capital, allowing lions and rhinos to roam against modern high-rise backdrops.

questions.question: What high-altitude Ethiopian capital city serves as the diplomatic headquarters of the African Union?
questions.explanation: Addis Ababa was founded in 1886 by Emperor Menelik II at the foot of Mount Entoto and sits over 2,300 meters above sea level.

questions.question: Which historic coastal capital city of Ghana was formed around seventeenth-century British, Dutch, and Danish trading forts along the Gulf of Guinea?
questions.explanation: Accra became the capital of the British Gold Coast in 1877 and continued as the national capital following Ghanaian independence in 1957.

questions.question: What is the average elevation in meters above sea level of Addis Ababa, making it one of the highest capital cities in Africa?
questions.explanation: Addis Ababa sits in the Ethiopian highlands at an average elevation of 2,355 meters, with northern sectors exceeding 3,000 meters.

questions.question: Which futuristic Persian Gulf metropolis is globally renowned for architectural icons including the Burj Khalifa and the Palm Jumeirah?
questions.explanation: Dubai grew from a small pearl fishing creek into a premier global hub for international aviation, finance, and record-breaking architecture.

questions.question: Which Middle Eastern capital city spreads across the southern slopes of the snow-capped Alborz mountain range beneath Mount Damavand?
questions.explanation: Tehran was chosen as the capital of Persia by Agha Mohammad Khan in 1786 and has grown into a metropolis of nearly ten million people.

questions.question: Which ancient Silk Road metropolis in Uzbekistan is world-famous for its majestic turquoise-domed madrasas on the Registan square?
questions.explanation: Samarkand served as the imperial capital of the Timurid Empire under conqueror Timur, celebrated for magnificent Islamic architecture.

questions.question: Which Saudi Arabian capital city grew from an isolated desert oasis walled town into a vast modern metropolis surrounding the historic Masmak Fortress?
questions.explanation: Riyadh is the political and financial capital of Saudi Arabia, home to landmarks such as the Kingdom Centre and Al Faisaliah Tower.

questions.question: Which hilly Levantine capital city was known in antiquity as Philadelphia and features a well-preserved Roman theatre in its downtown valley?
questions.explanation: Amman in Jordan was originally built over seven steep limestone hills and now spans over nineteen distinct urban hills.

questions.question: In what year was the United Arab Emirates officially formed, triggering the rapid modern transformation of Abu Dhabi and Dubai?
questions.explanation: Six emirates united under the leadership of Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan on December 2, 1971, with Ras Al Khaimah joining in early 1972.

questions.question: Which Asian megacity on the Buriganga River is ranked as the most densely populated national capital city in the world?
questions.explanation: Dhaka in Bangladesh packs over twenty-three million residents into its metropolitan territory, exceeding forty thousand people per square kilometer in central wards.

questions.question: Which two sovereign national capital cities face each other directly across the width of the Congo River as the closest pair on Earth?
questions.explanation: Kinshasa capital of the DRC and Brazzaville capital of the Republic of the Congo sit directly opposite each other on the Congo River.

questions.question: Which South American capital city is situated closest to the terrestrial Equator, located just twenty-five kilometers south of zero latitude?
questions.explanation: Quito is the closest national capital to the Equator, featuring the famous Middle of the World monument at zero latitude.

questions.question: Which major European capital was physically split into two distinct ideological sectors by a fortified concrete wall from 1961 to 1989?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall separated West Berlin from East Berlin during the Cold War until it was peacefully breached on November 9, 1989.

questions.question: What city on the Beagle Channel in Tierra del Fuego is commonly recognized as the southernmost city on Earth?
questions.explanation: Ushuaia in Argentina is the southernmost major city with over eighty thousand residents, serving as the main gateway to Antarctica.

questions.question: What is the approximate straight-line distance in kilometers separating the twin capital city centers of Kinshasa and Brazzaville across the Congo River?
questions.explanation: Kinshasa and Brazzaville sit only about four kilometers apart across the Pool Malebo expanse of the Congo River.
